image_description:
## 1. Chart type
A **faceted multi-panel line/area chart**. Each panel shows time-series lines for immunity levels, with a shaded horizontal band indicating the herd-immunity range.

## 2. Layout techniques
- **Faceting / small multiples**: 4 panels (Graph A–D), each representing a different scenario.
- **Layering**: Multiple lines, shaded area/band, annotations, and labels are overlaid within each panel.
- **No stacking**: The lines are not stacked.

## 3. Data variables

| Data Variable | Type of Variable | Visual Encoding |
|---|---|---|
| Time (months, Dec.–Dec.) | Temporal | Position on x-axis |
| Percent of population immune | Quantitative | Position on y-axis |
| Immunity type / series (e.g., Total immunity, Vaccine immunity) | Categorical/nominal | Color/hue and separate line series |
| Herd immunity range / threshold level | Quantitative | Horizontal shaded band position on y-axis |
| Scenario (Graph A, B, C, D) | Categorical/nominal | Faceting into separate panels |
| Threshold reached month (e.g., May, June, July, October, November) | Temporal | Text annotation/label at specific x-position with marker |
| Death estimate (e.g., 90,000; 100,000; 170,000; 200,000) | Quantitative | Text annotation in panel header/body |
| Scenario description (e.g., current pace, supply increase, ease up in spring, more contagious variant) | Categorical/nominal | Panel title/subtitle/header text |

comments.raw_comment:
Nowhere bear 170K would die if restrictions were lifted in April.  Why?
1. 50% of population (160M) have at least 1 shot.  120M fully vaccinated. 

2. Most vulnerable have been able to get vaccine for over a month.  84% 65+ had at least 1 dose

3. At least 160M already had/recovered (natural immunity). (32M "confirmed x 5 to account for untested=160M)

If you account for the fact that approx 1/3 of those w/natural immunity will get vaccine anyway that leaves an extra 110M to add to 160M vaccinated.

4. 110M+160M=270M which is approximately 82% of the U.S. population w/some form of immunity.
Even if you only use fully vaccinated it's 110M+120M = 230M which is  70%

5. The remaining unvaccinated people are "primarily" low risk people (or those who simply "choose" not to get vaccinated).  The death rate is ~0.03% for people "under" 60 (including the at-risk people).  After removing at-risk people from the data (because they've mostly been vaccinated) it reduces the death rate for the remaining "healthy" group to below 0.003%  (Yes, it's true.  Vaccinate the at-risk and you have a lot of "LOW RISK" people leftover.  Should be common sense).

That means 58M x .003%= 1,740K of those "healthy" people could die (NOT 170K).  Look at the CDC data per age groups and account for removing at-risk groups...

You're Welcome
Respect Logic/INTP's

These graphs make one assumption which is yet to be proven - that being infected with SARS-CoV-2 and recovering makes one immune for at least 1 year (first cases in early 2020).  The scenarios imply that roughly 35% of the population has been infected by mid-February 2021.  Given that the majority of those will have had no symptoms (asymptomatic) of or mild symptoms, you are suggesting that those folks will be immune.

We do not yet know the amount of antibodies and T-cells, etc., required to impart immunity.  SO the premise of this exercise would seem to have a glaring fault when predicting the date herd immunity will occur.

comments.raw_comment:
Pt.3 

There are many concerns surrounding the virus, but I see the biggest as the prominent amount of uncertainty. Ever since the start of it all, the public has been left with lingering questions upon when life will become normal again. The reveal helped me understand many parts of the article more clearly. At first, I was unaware of the difference that threshold immunity had compared to vaccine immunity. Many people, mostly between Democrats and Republicans, argued over the act of removing masks and what it could bring our country. I was unaware that threshold immunity is much more harmful than immunity formed by vaccines. It is only after a person receives both shots of the vaccines when they are announced fully vaccinated. This ultimately slows down the whole process of distributing vaccines, making it take much longer to reach the longed for threshold. After reading more information within the article, I also saw how total immunity includes the estimated number of those who contracted the virus and recovered from it. Even with the total immunity reaching its threshold in every chart, the deaths that will simultaneously occur are always much higher. This creates an inquiry for researchers of which plan is the most efficient way to take on the virus without too much hurt to the public.

Pt.1
More Restrictions Or Less Limitations. What Is The Right Call?
Once I reviewed the graphs detailed in this article, I noticed how obvious it is that Graph B is the most feasible and secure solution in order to reach the wanted herd immunity. Saying this, is this even an achievable plan? Even with President Biden's vision of having every adult in the United States vaccinated by May, many states lifted mask rules which could possibly set us back. Then again, is this act perhaps a step in a positive direction? Many debates are forming around this topic and the answer is unclear whether or not this risky move was beneficial. With disregard to the newly mask-less states, I can still see Biden's goal upon vaccines being reached. Teens, the most populated group of virus spreaders, are a huge factor to our goals. The vaccines are unable to cater to anyone under 16, leaving a vast portion of teens without the ability to get one. Even people the age of 16 who are eligible for the vaccine still have questions about it's safety. Will there be significant side effects that could possibly scare away many teens from receiving the vaccine? There are many concerns that I have, especially with Graph B and how it shows 90,000 casualties occurring if we are to reach immunity. It's also known in Graph D how unenlightened the United States is due to the possibility of new contagious variants springing up out of nowhere. How will scientists become aware of a new variant once it reaches us?

comments.raw_comment: In my first post, I said that I think that graph B is the ideal situation, which was correct. The graph reveal also showed graphs with even more vaccinations, to accelerate herd immunity even more, which is something I hadn’t previously considered(more than the 3 million in graph B). The huge vaccine increase pushes the total immunity up one month and the vaccine immunity up two months. It would also decrease the deaths by 10,000. Ending all social distancing precautions now would push the immunity timeline forward, but it would multiply the deaths by a little more than three. It is a very high-risk scenario and I do not think it’s the best option, especially when there are safer routes that have a closer timeline. Even easing up on the precautions in the spring could result in lots more unnecessary deaths. I wish that we could end all precautions now, however I know that is not the right path. We could have our lives back to normal now, but hundreds of thousands of people would be killed. The best option is to increase the vaccines as much as we can realistically and keep safety measures in place. If we can just hold out for a little longer the end could be very soon.

PART 1

More Restrictions Or Less Limitations. What Is The Right Call?

After studying these four graphs closely, it is clear to see that Graph B is the safest and fastest solution to reach the ideal threshold. However, how practical is this scenario? Although President Biden has made a promise to have every U.S. adult vaccinated by the end of May, states such as Texas, Mississippi, Iowa, Montana, and North Dakota have lifted mask restrictions with their states. Is this a move in the right or wrong direction? Is this the light at the end of a dark tunnel or a move taken too soon? At the current rate, vaccines are being distributed, I do believe Biden will uphold his promise. But the next concern is teenagers, argued the biggest group of spreaders for the virus. Testing is happening to ensure teens over the age of sixteen are able to receive the vaccine safely, but how long might this take? How many parents will allow their children to become vaccinated if it has potentially side effects? My biggest concern with the charts in the uncertainty. Graph B states that we could reach the herd immunity threshold by May, but in that time, 90,000 people could die. There is no way of knowing whether more contagious variants as displayed in graph D should be a concern or whether we are immune to all strains once vaccinated.

In my original response, I hit the mark in my discussion of how less precautions meant quicker immunity but more death, and that there is going to be a lot of deaths no matter which scenario plays out. I also noted that the immunity totals could very possibly be less than indicated because I know people who have had it twice. I failed to really analyze the other graphs and compare them to each other. Originally, I didn't even notice that the vaccine threshold is never reached in the variant scenario(Graph D).

After reading the reveal, I see that the graphs represent not only vaccine immunity, meaning the number of people who have been fully vaccinated, but also a total immunity including both vaccinated and those recovered from Covid-19. Each graph predicts when the immunity threshold will be met in four different circumstances. Using the strategies from this graph, the herd immunity would be reached the quickest with the least amount of deaths. I was also correct in the assumption that graph D would be the most risky option, increasing the death toll by nearly twice the current amount.

I think our best option is to try to increase the amount of vaccines given as much as we can , and very slowly start to reduce the number of public precautions that are put in place.

I thought easing up on precautions was ridiculous and fully unnecessary until more people were immune. But now, with the reveal of the graph, I see how dangerous it could be if we don't reach the herd immunity threshold before more contagious variants appear. This was shown in graph D. A mixture of C and B could actually be what decrease the number of deaths because of how many people would die if graph D came to fruition. Originally, easing up on precautions seem unreasonable, but easing up on just a few precautions along with a growing supply of vaccines.

comments.raw_comment: Looking at these graphs, I notice that there are different changes that we can make that will increase or decrease the amount of time that takes for us to reach herd immunity.  Consistently, total immunity increases at a similar rate to vaccine immunity.  There is definitely a positive correlation in those results.  I wonder why the total immunity and vaccine immunity both level off somewhere between 60 and 80 percent.  These graphs are hugely impactful on the entire nation.  I specifically think the captions with the graphs are informative, because they explain the great risks and loss of life we could endure, even if life gets to feel more normal and vaccines remain the same.  They help us to realize that this virus and its cure have a give and take element. These graphs display different ways to combat the coronavirus pandemic as quickly and normally as possible.  I could name this set of graphs, "Approaches to Ending the Coronavirus Pandemic, and the Risks We Take in the Process".

This impacts me and my community because COVID and the vaccines are happening pretty much everywhere right now. These graphs put into good perspective how we have to handle situations like this and a timeline for us to try to get it accomplished.

I truly wonder what direction the country would take from the four graphs displayed, and what specific laws/steps the government would take in getting to a closer threshold.

comments.raw_comment:
The first thing I noticed about the four graphs shown is that in order to accomplish herd immunity as soon as possible the most effective thing for our country to do is to try to increase the number of vaccines offered to people, and in the meantime keep the current public precautions in place. This would work very well if no new variants of the disease begin to spread. Based on the data, if the pace of the supply of vaccines is increased from the current amount of 1.7 million shots per day to 3 million shots per day, then it will be possible to reach the threshold of herd immunity by as soon as May. Out of all of the scenarios, graph B offers the most effective plan where most likely only 90,000 more people will die in between now and the threshold of herd immunity. 
I wonder how long the herd immunity of COVID-19 will last if as many people as possible get vaccinated within the next few months. Also, will there be another wave of a more severe strain of COVID-19 in the future?
Whichever scenario is chosen will have a large impact on my community and myself because if the wrong decision is chosen then the chance of getting the virus will be greater, and the chance of having stay-at-home orders will increase again. 
COVID-19: Increasing the supply of vaccines, Increases the chance of herd Immunity

comments.raw_comment:
I notice that these graphs look pretty similar at first glance, but really aren't at all. I don’t enjoy the graphical representation, but there's not a much better way to do it. I do enjoy how it shows the projected time that we will reach herd immunity. According to the graph, if we keep pumping out vaccines, and there are no coronavirus variants, and we keep the precautions in place, it’s the most ideal situation, where 90k people will die, but we will be immune by may. That would be amazing. 


I wonder if these graphs are really true. Trends change all the time and don’t follow data every time. The data is probably not 100% accurate, but whatever. Also, we don’t know that if you catch coronavirus, you are truly immune. So we should definitely try to stick to the vaccine at the moment, and see where that gets us. Additionally, I believe that we should try to ease up the lockdown even when we allegedly hit “herd immunity.”

The impact this has on our community is amazing. The more vaccines we pump out, the better. We’re pumping out so many vaccines at the moment that I think we’ll hit herd immunity around July. But that’s just my opinion. Maybe it’s different, maybe it’s not. But we’ll just have to wait and see.

My headline for these graphs are: When do experts think coronavirus will end based on these trends?

Hopefully the future is brighter and we have a situation like B play out, so we can get back to normal as soon as possible.

comments.raw_comment:
I noticed how these graphs relate to something regarding the covid-19 pandemic. More importantly, it focuses on the vaccination in different situations. These situations include its current supply, the supply increase, and public precautions. As shown in the graphs, the results for the total immunity from each graph are increasing much more than the result from the vaccine immunity.

I wonder how long it will take for everyone to receive the vaccination. We’ve been dealing with this pandemic for so long, we start to think that it might be a part of our daily lives. If the vaccine were to suddenly arrive at our doorstep, we’d take the chance to use it no matter what. But even so, we’d still have to wear masks if some people didn’t take the vaccine because of superstition, allergic reactions, or any other reason.

This impacts all of us in a way that tells us “Hey! You’re getting the vaccine soon!”. It gives us extreme joy knowing that we would no longer have to wear masks or use social distancing. We could soon return to the life we had before the pandemic hit us. But that doesn’t mean it happens now. It only takes a matter of time before we receive such a blessing.

The catchy headline I decided to give this article is “Covid vaccines: Quick as a hare or slow as a tortoise?”

This has a big impact on my community because I go to a school where people are crammed in halls and we sit in classrooms for hours upon end. I also live in a neighborhood where there aren't many people to interact with so I don’t have many problems with it at home.

comments.raw_comment: After examining each graph closely, I've determined that the best option, in my opinion, would be B. In theory, it would save more lives, however, I am skeptical of the government being able to vaccinate mass population efficiently.  It appears that many states are prepared to lift restrictions as those that already have. I think the majority of Americans have grown tired of the mask mandate as well as the restrictions on gatherings.  I feel as though many people would prefer option C, however, we must consider those who have underlying health conditions.  If there was certainty that the vaccination would be effective against each variant of COVID-19, then Graph D would be a possibility, although there are no guarantees. If the vaccines show that they are not working on each variant then they will probably slow the production of the vaccine. This would mean delays in reaching  herd immunity. Although graph A would eventually work, It would most likely take longer for everyone to either become immune or get vaccinated. One downfall to all of these plans is that the vaccines in question are not FDA approved, presently they are just approved for emergency use. This shows the government is unclear as to  the long term effects these vaccinations could have on people. The lack of proven data and uncertainty surrounding the vaccination have many Americans opting out of vaccination.

comments.raw_comment: Graph B is definitely the preferable graph out of them all, but it is unlikely that will reflect what actually occurs. Something I noticed is that Graph B is the only graph that shows a vaccine supply increase, and has the least amount of deaths because of that. It’s likely that Graph C will represent the path we take since some governments have been eager to lift restrictions and some have already done so. Graph D is also possible, but I wonder if other contagious variants would affect vaccine production and distribution, and by how much, if at all. I don't know if the other COVID-19 strains, such as the one discovered in the UK, could affect the production of vaccines. The impacts that these graphs show depend on the state of precautions and restrictions. If they are eased, social life will be a bit better for many, since there won’t be as many restrictions on what can or cannot be done. If they are not eased until vaccines are more widely available or until we reach some form of a herd immunity, then life will probably be the same for many as it has been for almost a year. A headline for these graphs could be; “The many paths to herd immunity.”

comments.raw_comment:
I noticed that in any scenario, there will still be thousands of deaths occurring. The three factors that the graphs take into account are vaccine supply, public precautions, and variants. I wonder if this is because these are the three biggest factors for herd immunity. The best case would be to have a vaccine supply increase, public precautions, and no variants. Although this is the most optimal, it's unlikely that there will suddenly be an increase in the vaccine supply. In that case, the best scenario would be to continue the current pace, with the current vaccine supply, public precautions, and no variants. I'm curious as to why someone would want to ease up public precautions in the spring. Spring doesn't mean that the virus is any less contagious or fatal as is. I wonder how these trajectories would change considering anti-vaxxers. 

This impacts me and my community because the pandemic as a whole has affected everyone in many different aspects. The biggest thing right now is herd immunity, with many places pushing to be open at full capacity, including fully reopening schools. These graphs provide a base of where the future is headed. They also show that the pandemic is still not over and that people need to take precautions seriously. 

A headline could be, "Where We Stand with COVID: The Quickest Way to Herd Immunity".

comments.raw_comment: The graph shows the cruel reality we currently live in. We have to choose between not having restrictions and risking the lives of others. It should be an easy answer to choose protecting others, but with the mental toll that this virus has caused it has people craving for things to be normal. If we choose plan B we will continue to live our current lifestyle which will be frustrating, but it will also save lives. The chances of us being able to successfully achieve plan B are slim. People have a tendency to do what benefits them rather than others so we will most likely end up leaning more towards plans D or C. We all should make an attempt to come together and in turn stop the virus, save lives, and get us back on our feet as fast as possible.

comments.raw_comment: By the evidence presented in these graphs, as the rate of shots administered per day increases, the amount of potential deaths decreases. Ideally, our goal as a collective, should be 3 million shots per day as shown in graph B. However, the main problem is that these goals may be too unrealistic and may not align with our current situation given the presence of variants. Because of the new rise to potential COVID variants, graphs A or C may be a more realistic outcome. To prevent further COVID deaths in the recuperation period, it is important to administer as many vaccines to the public as possible.

comments.raw_comment:
HERD IMMUNITY COMING SOONER THAN EXPECTED?
I notice that there are four scenarios of four graphs, of different ways that we could find herd immunity by a certain time of the year. I am drawn toward graphs A and B, particularly because they seem the best and the soonest immunity reached. Graph B is the best case scenario but it will be hard to reach that because vaccine supplies are hard to increase. Graph A seems more realistic and is my guess for the future. I believe that we should do everything in our power to end this whole thing as soon as possible and take every precaution to do so. I personally dislike online school and am ready to get back to learning face to face so gaining herd immunity before my Junior year would be great. I would still have 2 years left of high school, and plus those are the two best years. If we can all get through this by June or November and finally have a normal summer I would be ecstatic.

comments.raw_comment: I notice that using public precautions as well as increasing the number of people being vaccinated is seems to be the most beneficial approach to reaching herd immunity (70%+). Easing up on public precautions increases the number of deaths and lengthens the time to reach herd immunity (40 % to 70%). An increase in vaccine supply shows to be the most effective in reaching herd immunity sooner and preventing more deaths. I wonder if these graphs take into account individual states lifting restrictions, or if it is talking about the country as a whole. Will the results be different if everyone is acting inconsistently (states all doing different things)? This impacts the safety of my (and everyone's) community. As a student this impacts how quickly I can get back to a safe and normal schooling experience. The pandemic highly impacts schools and students physical and mental health. I think that keeping precautions/restrictions will save more lives, and increasing vaccine supply will bring the pandemic to an "end" sooner. I would headline these graphs "How Can We Make Covid 'Disappear' Sooner?".

comments.raw_comment:
Looking at these graphs, I imagine that we’d all want Graph B to be the true scenario. More vaccines, the same public precautions, and no variants. We’d reach herd immunity by May, and vaccine immunity by July. But truthfully, I am not sure how possible this is. With states that have as large of a population as Texas reopening in a crucial part of the pandemic, I highly doubt we will reach herd immunity before the summer. I think Graph C will closely model what actually happens. As I mentioned before, when states like Texas open up and get rid of mask mandates, in no way does that put us, as a country, anywhere closer to overcoming the pandemic. 

	I am also not sure of how spring break will affect these graphs. In Graph C’s scenario, lifting restrictions along with the massive influx of college kids to Florida (which has never had a mask mandate) is a recipe for disaster. It raises a few questions in my mind. Will we see a spike around the first week in April? Or, in some miraculous turn of events, will people stay at home? How quickly can we bounce back from the inevitable spike in cases/deaths due to people vacationing for spring break?

comments.raw_comment: These four graphs depict different possibilities of getting to herd immunity with the Corona Virus. While "herd Immunity" starts with just 70% of the population, we are only at approximately 40% immune (as a population). Looking at this chart, it makes sense that "vaccine immunity" will reach that 70% mark later than "total immunity" would because every day people are developing covid antibodies, and this line includes vaccinations. What's been consistent with each graph is the fact that the new mandates for the virus will most likely end this year, in 2021, with the earliest "total Immunity" being May, and the latest being July. I've also noticed that in each chart, the "total immunity" line levels off just above 80% immune, which makes sense because not everyone in the US will be exposed to covid to not everyone can be immune to covid. Whats's interesting to me is that there are only four graphs. I would like to depict and see the other possibilities to compare and contrast the "total Immunity" rate, the death rate, and the vaccines per day rate. I think these are the most important "numbers" throughout all these charts, and they tell us what the timeline will be, and how successful the scenario will be when it comes to making out with everyone alive.

comments.raw_comment:
Part 1:
 In these graphs, the first thing I noticed before I read about them or learned what they were representing was how similar they looked. The curves are similar and represent almost the same months. Going further and researching what they represent, I find it frightening that they are so similar even though they represent significantly different scenarios. I also notice how it is inevitable that thousands of American citizens will die. In each graph a certain number is predicted to die, a high number that is horrifying and unable to be stopped. I wonder how much information these graphs are taking into account. There will be spikes of cases around holidays and there may be periods where the cases falter and we see less. There are so many factors that could affect this such as issues with the distribution of the vaccine. It makes me question the reliability of the graph and makes me feel desperate for a solution to stop this disease that we’ll never find. These charts impact the precautions my community takes. Are they going to ease up on precautions to raise herd immunity but risk more people dying? Or will they keep strong precautions but the ability of herd immunity will go down? I believe we need to keep strong regulations in place for covid to ensure that people are not exposed until the vaccine has been distributed to them.

comments.raw_comment: These 4 graphs represent when the US will reach herd immunity under different circumstances. When we reach herd immunity we will be able to live a normal life again and Covid-19 will be spreading as much anymore and we will become much safer. Each graph shows different results from different ways of handling it. Graph A shows that if we continue at our current pace, we will reach herd immunity by July with around 100,000 people dying from the virus in that time. Graph B shows that we will reach herd immunity by May if we start to give out 3 millions shots per day, and only around 90,000 people will die from the virus. Graph C shows us reaching herd immunity by June if we end restrictions in April with our current vaccine supply, but around 170,000 people would die. Graph D shows us reaching herd immunity by July with our current vaccine supply, but with more contagious variants, and 200,000 people could die from the virus. I notice that each graph still has tons of people still dying from this virus. I wonder if there is a way that we could lower the death rate, so less people will lose their lives. This is very good for me and my community. This makes me very happy to think about.

comments.raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I  noticed that in the different scenarios, there’s one option that seems to be the best one on paper. That option is Graph B. To reach the maximum herd immunity threshold by May, the number of vaccinations would have to almost double. Also, according to that plan, restrictions would stay in place until that threshold is reached. I also noticed that each of the plans estimated that herd immunity would be reached by summer. Like I said, the ideal course of action would be plan B because it saves the most lives in the shortest amount of time. However, it keeps the US from going all the way back to normal for longer and it doesn’t include the possibility of variants. 
What do you wonder?
I wonder how these charts were made. What formula was used? They all seem to say that the end is near and that we could be at threshold immunity by July, but what can really back up that claim? While I hope that the graphs were correct, I can’t bring myself to believe it. I remember a year ago, everyone thought that we would quarantine and isolate for two weeks and  that life would go back to normal, and things obviously didn’t go that way. I also wonder if young adults and teens will be vaccinated under these plans. While I know adults and older people will have gotten vaccines, where does the younger population fit in?

1/2

comments.raw_comment:
What do you notice?
I notice that the pathways depicted in Graphs A and B will result in the least amount of deaths. I also notice that no matter which path depicted in the graphs is ultimately taken, it is expected that America will reach herd immunity by the summer. The most ideal scenario is that we increase our vaccination rate from 1.7 million shots per day to 3 million shots per day. If this occurs, America will experience the least amount of deaths (90,000) and will also reach herd immunity at the fastest rate (by May).

What do you wonder?
I wonder what mathematical formula and/or calculations were used to formulate these graphs. Even though all four graphs predict that we will reach herd immunity by July at the latest, I wonder if this will really come true. 

What impact does this have on you and your community?
Like every other community in America, COVID-19 has effected ever single person's way of life. Many people I know are truly tired of following COVID-19 protocol, but feel as if there is no end to the pandemic in sight. However, this graph might offer hope to many people in my community once they see that in almost every scenario, we will reach herd immunity in the next 6 months. 

Write a catchy headline that captures the graph’s main idea.
The End is Near!

comments.raw_comment: Many people in my community are not as cautious when it comes to being safe. As I look around town, I see large crowds of people huddled together, without masks or social distancing. Even with mask restrictions in place, COVID cases are still rising, and people don’t even follow restrictions. I understand how people who are vaccinated may think they are immune to getting the virus, but they should still be masking up, for the sake of others and for themselves. If we lifted restrictions like Texas has, the impact of the virus would increase significantly, and the rate of vaccinations would not be able to restrain the virus from spreading. In the graphs, we see different ways we can reach herd immunity, but the question posed is how. I believe if we can increase vaccine supply, keep the same public restrictions in place, with everyone following them, and having no variants, we could very well reach herd immunity by June, assuming everyone is able to get fully vaccinated. A catchy headline for these graphs: The Road to Immunity, Soon or Never? PART 2

comments.raw_comment: The first thing I noticed about the graphs were the death counts. With more than half a million Americans dead from the pandemic, I think it should be a top priority to keep that number as low as possible. I also noticed how the conditions of each graph changed, and how that reflects what could happen in the near future. In states like Texas and Mississippi, where restrictions are being lifted, we may see results similar to graph C, which will lead to many more Americans dying. In my opinion, we should do our best to stay on a model reflected by graphs A and B. Graph B is the ideal situation, but current vaccine supplies are unlikely to support 3 million people a day. I also noticed how much steeper the orange dotted lines are in graphs C and D. It is important to notice these lines because they show the population that will be immune due to exposure and recovery. It is a very poor choice to lift restrictions at the moment, as our death toll could rise like graphs C and D, especially considering the new strains of the virus that could be more deadly or contagious. My biggest wonder from this graph is how people will respond to it. The governor of Texas would likely benefit from seeing this graph. I think he would respond negatively to it, as he would see what could happen to his population. I also wonder how the virus deniers might view the graph. Would they experience a change in perspective if they were told the risks? It isn’t likely, but we would all benefit if they did.

comments.raw_comment: I noticed that there are many factors that go into the decision-making of this virus and how we might stop it. There are many different scenarios that would help others but hurt others. One of them being lifting public precautions. To the people who are vaccinated at the time and are healthy, this should not worry them but for someone who has underlying illnesses or has not receive their vaccine yet, they are more at risk. But when you look at all the plans you cannot avoid the fact that people are going to die from 90,000 to 200,000 people. I wonder what will happen if there is another spike in cases. Will we have to back to lockdown? Will easing up in the spring possibly lead us to shutdown? This could impact me and my community greatly. All of these are potential solutions and if we choose the wrong one it could lead us to another lockdown and more importantly many people dying. Is it really worth going back to normal and gaining deaths rather than waiting and possibly avoiding these deaths. Now we will never be able to avoid people dying but we can prevent it by taking the best precautions to keep us safe. I know my town has many small businesses that could not undergo another shutdown. These businesses getting back on their feet the last thing they need is it be told they are shutting down again. The graphs are showing us how long it will take for us to reach herd immunity with different precautions. A catchy title could be "There is hope and it is called immunity."

comments.raw_comment: In the charts I observed, I noticed how Graph B is the most reasonable way to continue on with trying to reach herd immunity.  It has the least amount of people that would die from the virus, and it also shows us reaching total immunity in May. Another plus about this graph is how many vaccines will be given out each day. With three million shots given each day, it shows us ending this global pandemic very soon which is a very pleasing thought. One thing about these graphs that makes me wonder is how did they know how many people would die from each scenario? I'm sure they based it on how many covid deaths occur daily but sometimes I am not always willingly trusting everything the media says. Something that surprised me in Graph 1 was how we would still be letting 100,000 people die if we continued distributing vaccines and keeping the mandates in effect. I guess most of those deaths will be from elders or people who are traveling a lot around the globe. The impact of someday reaching herd immunity will greatly impact my community, due to how we will be able to gather just like before the virus started. It will be refreshing to not have to wear a mask anymore and I feel like people will be in better spirits as well. Activities based on getting our community together will hopefully happen more and this will help the many kids who have been dealing with online learning. Getting out of the house and helping our community is such an important thing that everyone should practice.

comments.raw_comment: When looking at all four graphs, I noticed how the total immunity threshold is reached before the vaccine immunity threshold. It would make sense that the number of people who have recovered from the virus and have received the vaccine reaches the herd immunity range before the number of people who have been fully vaccinated, but this makes me wonder: how many people are going to suffer from the virus before we can all get vaccinated? We should take into consideration Graph B and how there is a smaller death toll when there is an increased vaccine supply. The last thing we should do is lift precautions, especially in spring when children are out of school and travel, because Graph C shows the largest spike in cases, other than Graph D, in which case, contagious variants are not anything we can change. If we keep precautionary measures while people are getting vaccinated, there will be less deaths during the total time it will take to get everyone fully vaccinated. Many people are also hesitant about getting the vaccine because of their thoughts on the virus, so how can we make sure that everyone that can get a vaccine, gets vaccinated? Another issue stands: children’s vaccinations. Since the vaccines that are being distributed are only safe for children over a certain age (16), how will we reduce the spread of COVID in children who are not of age to get vaccinated? Will there ever be a safe and effective vaccination for children to get? PART 1

The more we progress with the vaccines and the achievement of herd immunity these graphs give problem solvers in order to create a path for early succession but if we manage to fall down then this can end badly. My headline: "The Obstacles Towards Reaching Herd Immunity".

What do you notice?
It is clear that no matter what choice is made, more than 90,000 people are going to lose their lives. When looking at graph A and B, the 90,000 to 100,000 deaths don't seem as disturbing as the 200,000 people in Graph D that are going to die in the process of getting the vaccine. I notice that if the President goes with the data in Graph B, he wouldn't have to lift any precautions, reach herd immunity quicker, and still have more people vaccinated than those that will die.  

What do you wonder?
Since there are three variations of the vaccine, I wonder what the graphs would look like if they included which vaccine is being administered. 

What impact does this have on you and your community? 
I'm a child care worker so every day, I'm risking my family's health by going to work. COVID has caused a divide between everyone because there are people who don't believe in wearing a mask and then there are those that wear a mask as a means of protecting themselves and others. It's hard for me to go outside and to other places knowing that there can be someone that doesn't care enough to protect others. 

What's going on in the graph? Write a catchy headline for the graph. 
Since the graph is focusing on immunization, I would title this graph as "The Road to Immunization: The Rate of Vaccination and Rising Death Toll"

comments.raw_comment: Before reading this article I never knew how much really went into this pandemic. I have never been very good at charts, but all of them look very familiar in the way that they all are going up at what looks like the same rate which I can’t tell if that is good or bad. Something I did observe that is kind of scary is that there is no chart where people are not going to die. I also thought it was extremely interesting that the rate goes up a lot more in the summer I guess because everyone is going to be outside. With that being said I am curious if the weather has anything to do with the virus expanding. I also wonder why we are mass producing the vaccine if we already have a formula for it. It has an enormous impact on my community and myself. In a way it has almost taken away my high school experience which is a bit dramatic but something that has seemed to upset me. It has started to become very overwhelming and boring to sit in my room, stare at my computer and do work every day five days a week. I find myself getting very distracted and closing my computer to take unnecessary breaks. Which has had an overwhelmingly negative effect on my personal well being.

comments.raw_comment:
(Part 3) 

The pandemic has not only affected the economy of the whole United States and has caused the need for the creation of detailed plans, but it also has impacted the lives of many families, including mine. My mother, a Psychiatric Nurse Practitioner, has been forced to increase her hours at her practice just to fit the needs of the people in our community struggling with their mental health. The upbringing of people who previously did not carry any mental issues who are now flourishing with internal pain is insane. Luckily, it has kept my mother in a stable job, helping provide for our family. Some of my neighbors and friends do not have this privilege and their parents have been out of jobs ever since last March. So many struggle with the impacts of the pandemic, even the little things. Hence, we need to work together to spread recognition of the vaccination and aim to continuously follow guidelines to keep everyone safe. 


Headline: 
A Pandemic Diverged Into Four Roads, Which One Will it Take?

On the other, these graphs don't factor in those that refuse to take the vaccine so in some communities this could mean that it will take longer to reach immunity.

comments.raw_comment: The four graphs detailed in this article each show possible scenarios of how the pandemic will most likely run its course until reaching herd immunity. The graphs are easy to comprehend, visually presenting the rates of fatalities and gained immunity as the vaccine begins to be distributed. Saying this, all four plans show major fatalities within the United States, expecting at least 90,000 deaths to occur disregarding the chosen plan. With our current pace of vaccinating 1.7 million citizens each day, it’s projected that our country will reach full immunity by July of 2021 with around 100,000 deaths alongside the progress. There are other plans with ideas consisting of increasing the number of vaccines given out each day to help speed up the recovery of the country, but they still don’t cover the possibility of a new contagious variant that we do not have the technology to fight off.

comments.raw_comment:
"The Path for Herd Immunity"
Looking at the graphs we noticed that each of the graphs simulated how each of the vaccine and public policies were handled. The graphs show total immunity to the virus compared to just vaccine immunity. We also noticed that The threshold no matter what decision is made is still projected around May, June, or July. With increasing the supply of vaccines per day the projected amount of casualties becomes less and the threshold will come sooner. The Vaccine immunity is significantly lower than the total immunity. 

As a group we wonder, if more people will feel moved to get this vaccine if Covid was an even more deadly disease? How much would it cost for the government to give out 3 million doses each day? How is herd immunity calculated? How many states will ignore covid death toll predictions and end their restrictions early? Do the graphs account for people who are not going to get vaccinated? How would the graphs differ if done state by state?

This impacts our community because it might determine what's best for our future with the fewest casualties. This can impact government decisions on how the vaccine is distributed. The amount distributed can also help with foreign aid across the world to help other countries that may be struggling as well.

comments.raw_comment: In graph A, I noticed that the United States will reach herd immunity by July. We risk losing 100,000 people until that time. This affects me and the peers in my community because July is the heart of summer. This makes me wonder if the death toll will be higher, or lower because at that time more people will be vaccinated. Graph A is the most likely to happen if we continue to apply adequate public precautions. It represents our current pace of 1.7 million vaccines per day, and when looking at it I felt a sense of hope because I can finally see the finish line. But because the virus is unpredictable, there are other scenarios that can play out. In graph B, if the United States increased the distribution of vaccines to three million vaccines per day, we could reach herd immunity by May. Although this result would be fantastic, and the predicted death rate would reduce by 10,000, it is unlikely because we would have to nearly double our vaccine outtake.  In graph C, if restrictions were ended in April, the United States could reach herd immunity by June. Despite heard immunity being reached faster, we risk losing 70,000 more people without public precautions. This makes me wonder if we will wait until after herd immunity to end restrictions. Graph D represents predicted herd immunity with the added factor of disease variants. Diseases constantly evolve, so we can never be 100% accurate. My catchy headline for these graphs would be: Spring migration towards heard immunity.

comments.raw_comment: (Questions 1 and 2) By looking at the graphs I noticed that the total immunity threshold is reached before the vaccination threshold on all four of the models.  This makes sense because the total immunization accounts for the total number of people who have been vaccinated as well as the people who have recovered from the Coronavirus infection.  I also noticed that on Graph C, the one with the lifted restrictions beginning in the Spring, the total immunity threshold is reached faster than it is reached on any of the other graphs.  I assume that most of the total immunity for Graph C is coming from people who are recovering from the infection, considering that with lifted public precautions, the disease is more likely to spread.  I know that the graphs are showing herd immunity levels, which would include children and adults, but I wonder if they are factoring in the uncertainty of vaccinating children.  There is not a vaccine ready to be administered to children yet, and if the vaccine is proven to be unsafe for children, I wonder how the graph will be altered.  I also wonder which graph is the most likely path by which the immunization in the United States will occur.  I know that there is great reluctance among many Americans to take the vaccine, so how would the herd immunity be affected if a large sum of people were not willing to get vaccinated?

comments.raw_comment:
I notice that increasing vaccine distribution could help lower cases and increase the speed we reach the herd immunity threshold. In graphs A, C, and D, deaths are projected to increase dramatically if vaccines aren’t distributed and covid precautions are lifted, and the herd immunity threshold will be met much later.
The best plan to achieve herd immunity and minimize deaths is shown in Graph B. Graph B shows the effects of upping vaccine distribution to 3 million shots per day, provided there’s no new strain of virus. Doing this would mean reaching herd immunity by May, and experiencing 90,000 deaths. Increasing vaccination rates means we could reach the herd immunity threshold sooner. 
	These outcomes make me wonder how soon we will be able to attain herd immunity, if at all. Vaccine distribution seems to be increasing, but if we lessen precautions, it could make them useless. 
	The impact this has on my community is an impact on their safety. If we can increase vaccine distribution, it would mean less people die or are infected, ensuring our safety and the safety of others. 
Title: Race for Immunity

comments.raw_comment:
“Herd Immunity: Is it Coming Sooner or Later?”

Our group gathered a lot of information from these graphs. For one, in 3 out of the 4 scenarios, herd immunity would be reached by early summer or June/July. We also noticed that herd immunity is achieved when a little under 70% of the population is completely vaccinated and it is projected to happen over the summer according to the graphs. Even with easing some restrictions, we could reach herd immunity by June, but it means a lot more people will die. Lastly, by increasing the vaccine rollout from 1.7 million to 3 million shots per day, we could prevent 10,000 deaths. Our group wondered many things from these graphs, such as will the number of deaths start to decrease as many people are starting to get the vaccine. In addition, we wondered if our country increases the supply of vaccines, how would this affect us financially, and can we distribute more vaccines. The impact that this topic has on our community is that we have been dealing with COVID-19 for a year now and having herd immunity would be a big step into getting things back to normal. Also, it is a really big deal to get the vaccine to prevent more deaths and more people from getting sick. This graph also impacts our community because it shows how COVID-19 has greatly affected the world and how wearing a mask is important.

comments.raw_comment: Based on the data from the four graphs, our group noticed how each potential scenario could have a major effect on deaths and reaching herd immunity. If the supply of vaccinations increases from 1.7 million shots per day to 3 million shots per day, we could reach herd immunity in May rather than June. COVID variants with the current supply of vaccines would result in more deaths compared to maintaining the current supply and lifting restrictions. Although total immunity is currently around 40 percent, the overall vaccine immunity is lower. Based on these findings, we wondered, if we increase vaccinations by almost double, why will the herd immunity threshold only be met a month earlier? Lastly, how will distributions nearly double almost immediately if graph B were to be implemented? The virus has had a major effect on our communities but also the world as a whole. The deaths caused by the virus as well as the subsequent shutdowns has had a negative effect on both the population as well as the economy. The various plans for vaccination and reopening can potentially affect how many more people are lost due to the virus and when businesses, schools, and many other important organizations can reopen. We would name the title of this article, “A Light at the End of the Tunnel: How the U.S. is Approaching Herd Immunity.”

comments.raw_comment:
After studying these graphs, it’s apparent that there's no situation where deaths are completely preventable; they're going to occur regardless of the path we take. That being said, at first glance, Graph B seems to provide the best course of action. It shows that we could reach herd immunity by May, the earliest of all the predicted months, and estimates the least amount of potential deaths (~90,000). However, looking closer at this graph, I wonder at its probability/reality. It says in order to achieve these results, we would have to increase the supply of vaccines to 3 million per day, immediately. That’s nearly double what our current supply is (1.7 M), something that seems difficult to achieve promptly. As far as the impact these graphs and their trajectories have on my community and me, I’d say that Graph A, our current proceedings, seems most beneficial and would be the one I’d encourage us to stick with. I know everyone is anxious for things to return to normal, believe me, I am too, but when weighing the different aspects of each respective graph (timeframe, amount of potential deaths, the feasibility of actions), Graph A seems to provide the best balance. Compared to Graphs C and D, it has fewer deaths while also seeming more plausible than Graph B. The expected herd immunity of Graph A is reached in July, just like Graph D, but predicts fewer deaths than that graph. 
See 'Reply' for the continuation...

A headline for this graph could be “Planning out Precautions: What are the costs of taking longer to reach herd immunity?”

comments.raw_comment:
The graphs shown are showing the time it will take to herd immunity for the Coronavirus in the US. Herd Immunity means 70% – 90% of people are immune to the virus, whether through getting vaccinated or becoming infected and creating a natural immunity. Descriptions of what each graph is showing: 
Graph A: Current supply of vaccinations and public precautions
Graph B: Increasing the vaccine supply and maintaining public precautions
Graph C: Maintaining the vaccine supply with lifting some public precautions in the spring
Graph D: Maintaining vaccine supply and public precautions, but experiencing contagious variants 
All four of these graphs present different situations in which herd immunity is speculated to reach the 70%-90% mark. 
Graph B has the “most effective” situation. This scenario is upping the vaccine distribution count to 3 million shots per day instead of the 1.7 million in Graphs A, C, and D. It has the fewest deaths, 90,000, out of all four graphs. This graph also shows that the herd of immunity would most likely be reached by May. Graph D on the other hand is the “least effective” out of the four graphs. This scenario is saying that a more contagious variant will spread faster, therefore upping the herd of immunity. This graph is predicting the most deaths, 200,000, compared to the lower death toll of graphs A, B, and C. This graph is foreseeing the herd of immunity to be reached by July. I feel that a catchy title could be, "Herd Immunity: Now or Never?"

what I notice:
I notice that the U.S will reach herd immunity the soonest and if the vaccine supply increases, which also means fewer casualties.  This is shown in graph B. It is also clear that if the varients become more contagious, more people will die in order to reach herd immunity, about 200,000. This is shown in graph D. In graph C there is a similar death count to graph D when if we ease up on precaution in the spring, about 30,000 less than D. Finally in graph A I see that there is a similar death count to graph B when we continue precautions, have no varients, and the vaccine supply stays the same, about 100,000 deaths; 10,000 more than in graph B.

How it makes me feel/what do I wonder:
I wonder if we will actually reach herd immunity in the U.S. in July like the graphs shown or if this pandemic drag on much longer than expected. Will we be back in school full-time in August? The graphs show that the U.S. is slowly recovering from the virus, but the price is more death. The graphs make me hopeful for a future without this pandemic but also scare me because of how many more people will die in order to reach that threshold.

Finally, a catchy title for the graphs would be "The Race for Herd Immunity!" I think that this is a good title because each graph represents when in each scenario that we would reach herd immunity and the advantages and drawbacks of each of the four choices that we will have.

I've been constantly anxious about getting or spreading covid for a whole year now, and I know many people who feel the same. But the sad part is that we can't all comfort each other because that may put us at risk for infection.
These graphs are just showing the difference in vaccine and total immunity based on different factors. It shows what months we could reach total and vaccine immunity in but also when we can reach herd immunity. A good title could be "When Can We Herd in Herd Immunity."

comments.raw_comment:
Welcome to Wednesday's moderation of “What’s Going On in This Graph?”  

Today’s graphs show the results of a model that estimates when the U.S. will obtain herd immunity from the coronavirus.  (Herd immunity occurs when enough people become immunity to a disease to make its spread unlikely.  This is a result of vaccinations and natural infection.)   Here are graphs for four situations:  under current conditions, with increased supply of vaccines, with relaxing social distancing, and with more contagious variant spreads. 

From 9 am – 2 pm E.T. today, share with us your responses online to these three questions -- "What do you notice?",  "What do you wonder?", and “What impact does this topic have on you and your community?”

Plus, please share with us a catchy headline that captures the ideas in these graphs. 

By Friday morning, we’ll reveal the article that included these graphs and much more.  We look forward to reading your discoveries.

Note that you can get a link to your response to share with your teacher and classmates by clicking the response box below your response “Email me when my comment is published.”  

View our archives that link to past releases, organized by topic (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTopicIndex), 
graph type (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsTypeIndex) and 
Stat Nugget (tinyurl.com/NYTGraphsStatNuggetsIndex).  

Keep noticing and wondering.  The next graph on U.S. recent land development will be released by Friday, March 12 with moderation on Wednesday, March 17.

NOTICE:
If we keep the vaccinations at the pace we are currently in, herd immunity would be in July with 100,000 deaths, however, if an increase of vaccinations would go to 3 million per day, herd immunity would be reached in May with 90,000 deaths. If we were to ease up on restrictions and keep the current daily vaccination supply, then herd immunity would be in June with 170,000 deaths. If we were to have the current vaccine supply & more contagious variants, then the herd immunity would come in July with 200,000 deaths. 
The second graph shows that the combination of vaccination increases and the use of precautions in the public could expedite the arrival of herd immunity.
WONDER:
What kind of impact would increasing the supply of vaccines have on the country financially? 
Do these graphs take into account those who have had coronavirus and have a window of immunization?
Do these graphs take into account the population of people who will not follow restrictions? 
IMPACT:
This has a huge impact on me and my community because it is predicting how much time until we can all get back to “normal”. As someone in the education field, this virus has impacted my ability to have a “normal” field observation experience. These graphs that project herd immunity happening in the summer, give me the hope that the virus will be under control by the time I have another field observation in the fall. 
HEADLINE:
“Four different plans for COVID action. Which one will we follow?”

Holding similar conditions as Graph B, except for more contagious variants, the results drastically change. The number of fatalities could spike towards 200,000. While the threshold for total immunity would be reached in July, paralleling Graph A, the threshold for vaccine immunity would not be reached at all (unlike the 3 other graphs). Hence, Graph D presents the worst possible scenario. 

I wonder which plan the United States will take: whether the vaccine supply will be kept at the current pace or increased, whether public precautions will be kept or ended in April, and whether there were will no new variants or more contagious variants. The possibilities and results are vast and unpredictable.

I very much miss my life the way it was before the pandemic, and the intense waiting is very killer. I know I am doing my part to get this pandemic over with, and I hope that my community does the same. Potential headline: "How Soon Can We Return To a Normal Lifestyle?"

What do you notice?
I notice that summer is predicted to be when immunity levels begin to increase greatly. This is consistent in each scenario represented in the different graphs. I also notice that if we want to have the smallest number of deaths possible, the situation represented in graph 2 would be the most effective way to do this. This is hard to make possible, though, as we cannot control whether a more contagious variant appears in the US or not. Although graph 2 predicts the least number of deaths, 90,000 deaths is still an extremely high number, which is disconcerting.


What do you wonder?
I wonder why increasing the pace of the vaccines in graph 2 to almost twice as much as the pace in graph 1 would only save 10,000 lives. I also wonder what would happen if we increased the pace of the vaccines while keeping restrictions high but a more contagious variant appeared.


What impact does this have on you and your community?
This affects my age group specifically in terms of what will happen in the near future. We should be going to college in the fall, but I'm not sure how that will look thanks to COVID. I hope that college students will be able to be vaccinated before going to college, as that would make the process of transitioning to a new environment much less stressful.

comments.raw_comment:
I notice that the four graphs represent four possible ways in which the United States could reach herd immunity. The first graph shows what the future could look like if we continue with life as it is now: 1.7 million vaccinations a day with public precautions (social distancing and mask-wearing). The second graph shows a future in which 3 million vaccinations are given per day. In this possible scenario, we would reach herd immunity by May. The third graph shows what the future would look like if we continue with 1 million vaccinations a day, and then lift the restrictions in April. In this scenario, we would reach herd immunity faster, but with more deaths. The final example shows a future in which a more contagious variant spreads. In this scenario, it would take until July to reach herd immunity and up to 200,000 more people could die from the virus.

I wonder which scenario is most likely. I also wonder if the government plans on increasing their vaccination rates to 3 million shots per day, like in the second graph. I wonder if a more contagious variant has already begun to spread throughout the U.S. Finally, I wonder what exactly herd immunity entails. Does herd immunity mean that the virus vanishes completely?

This impacts my community because vaccinations mean less deaths and a return to normal life in my community. Covid 19 is abundant in my city and increased vaccination rates would help us all greatly.

Headline: Four Paths to the Normal World—But at What Cost?

What do you notice?
I notice that different variables can have large effects on when we can reach herd immunity. It is interesting how the supply of vaccines, public precautions, and variants can affect the time for the general public to reach herd immunity. It is really interesting that even with our great progress with vaccination if we ease restrictions in the spring an extra 70,000 people could die, but herd immunity would be reached a month earlier. It is also interesting how variants that are pretty much out of our control could significantly impact the timeline of herd immunity and deaths from the virus.

What do you wonder?

I am curious about how more infections lead to both earlier herd immunity and more deaths. How many deaths does each additional infection bring? How much earlier does it move up the herd immunity threshold? Does more infections lead to more chances for worse variants?

What impact does this have on you and your community?

These graphs show both when it may be safe to reopen, but also how many people will die from the virus in different scenarios. While we want to reopen sooner which would be good for our local economy, every death will significantly harm the family and friends of the deceased as well as hurt the industries they may work in or be supporting financially.

comments.raw_comment: These graphs represent the various possibilities and scenarios of vaccines, public precautions and variants of the virus.  The first graph shows the current situation where there are no variants and with the current number of vaccines the immunity threshold would be reached in July but in the meantime 100,000 people could die. The second graph illustrates the potential situation of an increase of 3 million vaccines always without variants you could reach the immunity threshold in May with 10,000 deaths. As for the third graph, it shows how with a loosening of the precautions during the spring and with the same dose of vaccines at this time we could reach the immunity threshold in June, however with 170,000 deaths. Finally, the last graph proposes a situation where variations of the virus increase with the same number of vaccines and taking into account public precautions. In this case, the immunity threshold would be reached in June but there would be twice the number of deaths compared to the current situation. In our opinion, the best option is illustrated in the second graph because we would reach faster the immunity threshold and less people would die.
